manifest.name: dsh-client-ui-usage-hud
manifest.description: A DeepSeek Harness sidebar HUD: account balance, gifted balance, cumulative spend and token usage, styled after the Abyssal Maid Atelier skin.

bundle.text:
# usage-hud bundle patch: inserts its own loader row, which serves both the
# host half (the /api/dsh/usage-hud JSON route) and, through `dsh.client`, the
# browser half (the sidebar widget). The name must match this package's own
# `name` field, because that is the specifier the Loader imports.
- insert:
    - id: ui-usage-hud
      name: 'dsh-client-ui-usage-hud'

readme.section: dsh-client-ui-usage-hud
readme.text:
A sidebar HUD for **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** that shows your account balance, gifted
balance, cumulative spend and token usage — always visible in the left sidebar foot.

Styled after the [Abyssal Maid Atelier skin][maid] (`@smalltailqwq/dsh-client-ui-skin-maid-atelier`,
深海女仆工坊): navy, gold and porcelain, Georgia serif, lace-edged glass panel. It reads
that skin's own published CSS variables and falls back to the same values when the skin
is not active, so it looks right either way.

readme.section: dsh-client-ui-usage-hud
readme.text:
[maid]: https://github.com/Small-tailqwq/dsh-deep-whale

```
                            ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
   footer trigger  →  🐋 ¥16.8287            │ 深海账户 · Token 用量        刷新 │
                       14,096万 tok          │ 账户余额              ¥16.8287 │
                                             │ 赠送余额               ¥0.0000 │

Collapsed, the trigger shrinks to a 34px round whale button.

readme.section: What it shows, and where each number comes from
readme.text:
| Row | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account balance | `normal_wallets` per currency | platform `GET /api/v0/users/get_user_summary` |
| Gifted balance | `bonus_wallets` per currency | same |
| Cumulative spend | `total_costs` per currency | same |
| Total tokens | sum of all four token buckets + session count | session projection cache, `tokenUsage.totals` |
| Last request | uncached input / cache read / output | same, `tokenUsage.last` |

readme.section: What it shows, and where each number comes from
readme.text:
Every money figure is read from the platform. Nothing is estimated, and no price table is
applied.

readme.section: Why this plugin has to talk to the platform itself
Why this plugin has to talk to the platform itself
readme.text:
The platform's own docs say the same thing: *"Host projects only ... normal_wallets /
bonus_wallets currency/balance strings; response tokens and other fields are discarded."*
That is why the shipped UI never shows cumulative spend — the data is there, DSH throws it
away.

So this plugin's host half obtains a platform credential and reads the same endpoint for
itself, parsing `total_costs`. Real response:

readme.section: Why this plugin has to talk to the platform itself
readme.text:
```json
{"code":0,"data":{"biz_code":0,"biz_data":{
  "normal_wallets":[{"currency":"CNY","balance":"16.8287497600000000"}],
  "bonus_wallets":[{"currency":"CNY","balance":"0"}],
  "total_costs":[{"currency":"CNY","amount":"9.3328969200000000"}]}}}

Amounts are decimal **strings** and are kept verbatim until formatting, so precision is
never lost to binary floating point.

readme.section: The credential API that actually works here
The credential API that actually works here
readme.text:
`inferenceOrigin` is `https://api.deepseek.com` — the *inference* origin. The account
endpoints live on `https://platform.deepseek.com`. Passing the platform origin therefore
returns `undefined` with no error, which reads exactly like "signed out".

readme.section: The credential API that actually works here
readme.text:
The correct accessor for the platform origin is `getPlatformSession()`, which returns
`{ origin, token, userId, requestHeaders }` and "exports the stored grant only when its
issuer matches `platformOrigin`". It also hands back the provider-owned client headers the
platform expects. This plugin uses that.

readme.section: Data flow
readme.text:
```
client.js ──GET /api/dsh/usage-hud──► lib/index.js
                                        ├─ deepseekAccount.getPlatformSession()
                                        │    └─ GET platform.deepseek.com
                                        │         /api/v0/users/get_user_summary

readme.section: Data flow
readme.text:
Token totals come from the **persisted projection cache**, not from live sessions, so cold
and archived sessions count too. The route also wraps the same response envelope the
account service does (`code` / `data.biz_code` / `data.biz_data`) and honours the same
`401` and `40003` invalidation paths, calling `rejectToken` when the grant is dead.

Nothing secret is exposed to the browser: the token lives only inside the host half, and
the route rejects cross-site callers.

readme.section: Requirements
readme.text:
- DSH with the `deepseek-account` platform plugin enabled and an **official account signed
  in**. In API-key mode there is no platform grant, and the money rows say so instead of
  inventing a zero.
- No third-party runtime dependencies. No build step — `lib/*.js` is hand-written,
  directly executable JavaScript.
- Works in light and dark themes.

readme.section: Install
readme.text:
A DSH bundle is a package whose `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`; DSH composes
its patch layer into the profile. Install it into a profile directory.

readme.section: Option A — plugin manager (uses pnpm and git)
readme.text:
```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add <this-repo-url>
```

DSH enables a newly installed bundle by default. Restart DSH once.

readme.section: Option B — manual (no pnpm, no git required)
readme.text:
1. Copy this directory into the profile's `node_modules`:

```
   <dshHome>/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-client-ui-usage-hud/
   ```

2. Append the package name to the profile's `package.json`:

```json
   {
     "dsh": {
       "profile": {
         "bundles": [

3. Restart DSH. The loader applies this bundle's `cordis.patch.yml`, which inserts the
   row `ui-usage-hud`, and serves `lib/client.js` to the browser.

4. Refresh the page.

readme.section: Making the host half hot-reload
readme.text:
By default DSH watch roots are empty, so editing `lib/index.js` needs a restart. To iterate
without one, add this plugin's directory to the `hmr` row in the profile's
`cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: hmr
  name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-hmr"
  config:
    root:

`lib/client.js` is polled by `dsh-client-hmr` already: a page refresh picks up changes.

readme.section: Layout
readme.text:
```
package.json          # dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client (platform: web)
cordis.patch.yml      # insert: ui-usage-hud
lib/index.js          # host half: the GET /api/dsh/usage-hud route
lib/client.js         # browser half: the sidebar widget

readme.section: Layout
readme.text:
The browser half is a browser artifact in DSH's lazy-CJS shape — it registers itself with
`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` and exports `apply` and `inject`. It uses
only the shared platform runtime (`require("react")`), mutates nothing outside its own
`[data-usage-hud]` scope, and removes its stylesheet on disposal.

readme.section: Verifying
readme.text:
There is no build step, so the tests run the shipped files directly:

```sh

readme.section: (no credentials needed: it feeds a fixed payload through a fetch stub)
readme.text: node tests/client-test.mjs lib/client.js

readme.section: drives the real route handler with a stub account service and calls the platform
readme.text:
node tests/host-e2e.mjs ./lib/index.js
```

`tests/client-test.mjs` loads the bundle exactly the way DSH does, provides a minimal React
hooks shim, opens the popover and prints its rendered text. It needs no account.
sh

readme.section: read the grant from your DSH profile
readme.text: node tests/host-e2e.mjs ./lib/index.js

readme.section: or hand it over explicitly, touching no file
readme.text:
DSH_PLATFORM_TOKEN=... node tests/host-e2e.mjs ./lib/index.js
```

readme.section: Notes and limitations
readme.text:
- Money rows reflect the **official DeepSeek account** only. On third-party provider
  routes they are unavailable, and the popover offers the platform usage link instead.
- The widget refreshes every 20 seconds and whenever the page becomes visible again, so
  the account endpoint is polled periodically.
- `total_costs` is whatever the platform reports; this plugin does not scope it by period.
  Compare against the platform's usage page for a per-day breakdown.
- Amounts are formatted with up to 4 decimals, or 2 above 1000, and sub-cent values show
  as `<0.01`.
